name: kube-score-06dedc9c-blind26-ots
instr:
# A Kubernetes manifest grading CLI giving wrong verdicts and mangled reports, diagnosed without a test suite

I use this command-line program to read cluster manifests written in YAML and get back a graded list of findings for each object in them, and with the current tree a large share of what it tells me is wrong. The repository has received 23 separate undocumented edits. Below is everything I managed to pin down by hand, written up by what I was doing when I hit it.

Just starting it already goes wrong. When I put a recognized subcommand word first on the line it is no longer resolved as that subcommand, and the number of leading arguments treated as consumed comes back wrong with it, so everything after them is misread. Started under its alternate executable name with nothing but a file path, it no longer falls back to its default checking behavior; started under its ordinary name, it acts as though it had been started under the other one. Telling it which cluster version to judge against fails too: a two-part number such as 1.18 is now rejected as malformed, while a three-part number such as 1.2.3 is swallowed without the refusal it used to get.

Feeding it files is unreliable. A file whose single document wraps several objects in a list no longer yields those objects at all — I get an empty result or an outright failure where every item in the list used to be examined on its own.
